proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 14^n is congruent to 14^(n mod 18) modulo 19.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 19.
The residue 14 has order 18 modulo 19: for every n in [0, 42], 14^(n+18) is congruent to 14^n modulo 19.
There exists an integer n in [1, 60] with n^2 > 60.
Every n in [0, 60] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 18.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 4. (the congruence established modulo 6 is carried over to modulo 4)
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 60].
For every n in [0, 60]: if 18 divides n then 14^n is congruent to 1 modulo 19.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 60 we have n^2 >= 2n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
Every integer n in [1, 60] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 60].
